delta.text: # Research Verdict
**Bottom Line:** Yes, localized defect-free regions of cubic boron arsenide
(c-BAs) reach a room-temperature thermal conductivity of ~1300 W/mK [
3], matching 2017 four-phonon theoretical predictions of ~1400 W/mK [2]. However, typical
chemical-vapor-transport (CVT) crystals suffer from severe defect-driven spatial nonuniformity that reduces macroscopic bulk performance
by an order of magnitude [5, 8], while recent ultra-pure synthesis efforts claim localized values exceeding 2100 W

/mK [11].

## theory predictions
In 2013, Lindsay et al. predicted
via three-phonon calculations that c-BAs achieves a room-temperature thermal conductivity exceeding 2000 W/mK [
1]. In 2017, incorporating higher-order four-phonon scattering reduced this theoretical prediction from 2200
to 1400 W/mK [2], though 2025 theoretical and experimental revisions remain
contested between 1060.51 W/mK and over 2100 W/m

K [10, 11].

## measurement history
In 2018, Kang et al
. reported a room-temperature thermal conductivity of 1300 W/mK in defect-free c-BAs regions [3], whereas
simultaneous studies by Li et al. and Tian et al. measured lower peak values of 1000 ± 90 W/mK and
1160 W/mK [4, 12]. Subsequent 2022–2
024 studies confirmed local conductivities between 1200 and 1300 W/mK alongside

high carrier mobility [7, 13].

## sample and method
While native impurities and defects typically suppress bulk c-BAs thermal
conductivity by an order of magnitude [5], some defect-bearing samples still exhibit 1000–130
0 W/mK [14]. Regarding time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) ballistic artifacts

(c6), the court is bound by the jury's rejection of methodological invalidation.

## commercial outlook
Optical
transient grating measurements confirm c-BAs simultaneously achieves 1200 W/mK thermal conductivity and 1600
cm²/Vs ambipolar mobility at the same locations despite spatial variations [7, 15]. Commercial wafer-scale
integration remains unfeasible because CVT growth is limited to ~1 mm crystals [8], though liquid-arsenic Bridgman growth is emerging

as a high-uniformity alternative [16].

## Contested & ruled
On c6, the Advocate showed
that TDTR apparent thermal conductivity drops with spot size due to ballistic transport [6], while the Skeptic showed no modulation frequency dependence between
1.2 and 9.3 MHz [9]. *Per human ruling: "rule for the counter-evidence" (note
: "auto-resolved (CLI)")*. Following this ruling, the tie-breaker on c7 confirmed 1200 W/mK
via optical transient grating [7] and 1300 W/mK in subsequent verification [13].
